summary:
Builder 4 is done. The full `lune run scripts/verify` is green: 718 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. Nothing is committed and Studio was not touched.

**S-PAR-02**
- **List:** `tests/fixtures/Parity.luau` holds every fixture of the repo in a fixed order. The 149 Adversarial variants come as drafts; both runners canonicalize them and drop the ones Canonical refuses (L17), so 43 are digested.
- **Lune digest:** `tests/Physics/Parity.spec.luau` blesses `tests/golden/parity.bv1.digest.txt` (131 bytes). Fixtures: 136 designs, fnv1a32 945249129. Generated: 200 designs, fnv1a32 440098388.
- **Per-design hashes:** a second golden, `parity_designs.bv1.golden.txt`, keeps each design's hash so that a Studio FAIL can be diffed against it.
- **Support:** `Golden.digest` writes `<name>.digest.txt` and refuses anything over 1 KB; Tol gains PARITY_DESIGNS and PARITY_SEED; FakeRoblox gains IsClient and the goldens as StringValues named by stem, the naming Rojo 7.7.1's sourcemap shows.
- **Snippet:** `tests/studio/e2e/S-PAR-02.luau` is proven on FakeRoblox by `tests/Physics/SPar02.spec.luau`. The full runs are slow cases (Server, Client, and the GROUP split); five failure-path cases are fast, 0.45 s. It was not run in Studio.

**SPEC and evidence**
- **[12]'s rows:** every edit is made, plus L4, L9, L10 and L15.
- **§17.1:** O7 now carries M3's measured figures. New O10 (D1) and O11 (D2) follow O9. Every **[Decision to confirm]** mark now has its number; the §13 mark "(§17)" became "(§17.1 O1)".
- **Evidence:** a new section, E-S2.13, holds M3's numbers. Its script is `docs/spec/prototypes/S2/m3/limits.luau`.

**Re-measured on this tree through `Analyze.run`**
- **L4's evidence:** the critic's proud-core figures reproduce to the digit.
- **O11's Y-shift figure:** Gen #131 at +0.2 moves Sharpening's G by 0.0037 through `Analyze.run` as built.

README's Layout and Status say M3 is built and S-PAR-02's Studio runs are pending. My section is at the end of docs/build/M3-notes.md.

deviations: Digest layout: one {bytes, designs, fnv1a32} entry per group under `analyze`, not [8.5]'s single {designs, fixtures, generated, bytes}, so that GROUP can compare one group alone.
Snippet lines: one `analyze` line per group, plus a `digest` line for the whole text (version included) when GROUP is 'all', instead of one line holding both hashes.

A second golden, parity_designs.bv1.golden.txt, keeps every design's fnv1a32, so a Studio FAIL's `hashes` lines can be diffed without running Lune. The snippet never reads it, since §14.2 says Studio reads digests only.
Between designs the snippet calls its 4 ms slice instead of an unconditional task.wait(). That saves about 336 frames (about 5.6 s) per Studio call.
On a FAIL, the per-design hashes are emitted as FAIL lines {check = 'hashes'}, 20 to a line. They are not counted as assertions, and the summary counts assertions only.
Parity.luau lists the A variants as {name = key, draft = variant.draft} entries, not bare keys. Both runners still canonicalize them and drop the refused ones, as L17 asks.
Golden gains readDigest beside digest, and check and digest share one comparison. Parity.spec adds a fast list check beside the slow digest.
SPar02.spec lives in tests/Physics as [11] says and requires ../ItemRender/FakeRoblox. Its full runs are t.slow (L17); its fast cases test the failure paths on short runs.

A new evidence section E-S2.13 and a folder docs/spec/prototypes/S2/m3/ (limits.luau, its output, a README), so the SPEC cites repo evidence rather than build notes. L4's figures were re-measured with Analyze.run instead of the emulator.

The SPEC carries measured values where the lead's text quoted the plan's emulated ones. L10's 'P1 28.5 (≈ 74)' becomes B3's 28.2 (≈ 73). O11 carries B3's 0.1250 plus a tier flip, with D2's 0.0236 beside it.
L4's 'Thinness carries 0.31–0.36' is written as 0.10–0.36 (all of it on 7 crossings), which is what all 12 crossings show; the critic's own c_proud2 already had 0.1038 on one of its three.
Outside M3's rows: I numbered §13's '(§17)' mark as O1, and corrected the O11 figure in Factors.luau's header comment (0.024 → 0.125 and a tier). Neither is code behaviour.
